findings.title: Individual admin permission resources are created without a resource type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource creates the resource with resourceStore.create(...) and updates its scopes, but never sets resource.setType(resourceType). ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission looks up resources with resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), so individually created client resources will not match type-based queries. This can make per-client grants invisible to code that enumerates clients by type, breaking client listing/filtering based on permissions.

findings.title: Existing realms are not migrated to the new Clients resource type and scopes
findings.body: init returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is not null. Realms initialized before this change therefore do not get the Clients type resource or the new configure, map-roles-client-scope, and map-roles-composite scopes. Subsequent client permission evaluation can silently deny access or fail because the schema expects those objects to exist.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when Clients type resource is missing
findings.body: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) calls AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately dereferences the result in authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource can return null if the Clients type resource has not been created, for example on an existing realm, causing a NullPointerException instead of returning false.

findings.title: Removed-entity cleanup is disabled for V2 and can throw if V1 and V2 are both enabled
findings.body: The provider-event cleanup is now gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. When only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, client removal no longer triggers cleanup, so authorization resources referencing removed clients can remain orphaned. If both features are enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and clients().setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException because ClientPermissionsV2 marks it unsupported.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle Clients resources
findings.body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type. For Clients resources it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), but client resources are created with the client ID as the name and no display name, and the type-level Clients resource has no label. This can leave permission/resource representations with null or meaningless names in the admin API/UI.

findings.title: No test exercises map-roles-client-scope
findings.body: The PR adds the map-roles-client-scope scope to the Clients resource type and implements canMapClientScopeRoles, but the added tests only cover map-roles and map-roles-composite. A wiring or evaluation regression for map-roles-client-scope would not be caught.
